questions.text: A body starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 2 m/s². How far does it travel in 5 seconds?
A current of 2 A flows through a 5 Ω resistor. Calculate the power dissipated.
questions.explanation: P = I²R = 2² × 5 = 20 W.

questions.text: Two resistors of 4 Ω and 6 Ω are connected in parallel. Find the effective resistance.

Calculate the heat required to raise the temperature of 2 kg of water by 10 K. [Specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J/kgK]
A wave of frequency 500 Hz has a wavelength of 0.6 m. Calculate its velocity.
A machine lifts a load of 800 N using an effort of 200 N. Calculate the mechanical advantage.
questions.explanation: MA = load/effort = 800/200 = 4.

questions.text: A machine with a velocity ratio of 5 has a mechanical advantage of 4. Calculate its efficiency.
Calculate the pressure at a depth of 5 m in water of density 1000 kg/m³. [g = 10 m/s²]
A body of mass 2 kg moving at 5 m/s collides with a stationary body of mass 3 kg and they move off together. Find their common velocity.
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved: 2 × 5 = (2 + 3)v, so v = 10/5 = 2 m/s.

questions.text: A radioactive substance has a half-life of 8 days. What mass of an 80 g sample remains after 24 days?
questions.explanation: 24 days is three half-lives: 80 → 40 → 20 → 10 g.

questions.text: Which of the following electromagnetic waves has the shortest wavelength?
questions.explanation: Gamma rays occupy the highest-frequency, shortest-wavelength end of the electromagnetic spectrum.

questions.text: An object is placed at the centre of curvature (2F) of a converging lens. The image formed is
options: real, inverted and the same size as the object
questions.explanation: At 2F the image is formed at 2F on the other side: real, inverted and the same size as the object.

questions.text: A cell of emf 12 V and internal resistance 1 Ω is connected to a 5 Ω resistor. Calculate the current in the circuit.
A force of 50 N moves a body through 4 m in a direction making 60° with the force. Calculate the work done.
If the length of a simple pendulum is increased four times, its period will
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(l/g), so T is proportional to √l. Quadrupling l doubles T.

questions.text: A semiconductor doped with a trivalent impurity such as boron becomes
questions.explanation: A trivalent dopant creates holes as the majority carriers, giving a p-type semiconductor.

questions.text: A gas occupies 200 cm³ at 27°C. At what temperature will it occupy 300 cm³ at constant pressure?
questions.explanation: Charles' law: V₁/T₁ = V₂/T₂ → 200/300 = 300/T₂ with T₁ = 300 K, giving T₂ = 450 K = 177°C.

questions.text: Which of the following is a fundamental quantity?
questions.explanation: Mass is one of the seven fundamental quantities; force, density and pressure are derived from mass, length and time.

questions.text: A body of mass 200 g occupies a volume of 40 cm³. Calculate its density.
questions.explanation: Density = mass/volume = 200/40 = 5 g/cm³.

questions.text: The area under a velocity–time graph represents the
questions.explanation: Velocity multiplied by time gives displacement, so the enclosed area is the distance travelled.

questions.text: The weight of a body on the moon is about one-sixth of its weight on earth because the moon has
options: a smaller acceleration due to gravity
a smaller mass for the body
questions.explanation: Mass is unchanged; weight falls because g on the moon is roughly one-sixth of g on earth.

questions.text: During a change of state, the heat supplied to a substance
options: changes its state at constant temperature
is entirely lost to the surroundings
questions.explanation: Latent heat breaks the bonds between molecules, so the temperature stays constant while the state changes.

questions.text: Sound waves cannot travel through a vacuum because they
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs particles of a medium to transmit the vibration.

questions.text: The image formed by a convex mirror is always
options: real, erect and the same size
questions.explanation: A diverging mirror always forms a virtual, erect, diminished image behind the mirror, which is why it is used as a driving mirror.

questions.text: In domestic wiring, the fuse is connected to the
questions.explanation: Placing the fuse in the live wire cuts off the supply from the source when excess current flows.

options: square of the distance between them
square of the product of the charges
questions.explanation: Coulomb's law states F = kq₁q₂/r², an inverse-square relationship with distance.

questions.text: The energy stored in a spring of force constant k when stretched through an extension e is
questions.explanation: Work done in stretching = area under the force–extension graph = ½ × (ke) × e = ½ke².
